last_research.summary: Approve bounded stock-coverage and buyer price-gap routing responses, while retaining the current operating policy and profile parameters. Stockouts (49 in 60 minutes) and 48 units of stock versus 198 median peer stock support a coverage response, though external trade rate is essentially flat and a discoverability block is recorded. Goods conversion is weak (5/43 closed orders paid) and 61/62 goods quotes were above cap; route qualifying repeated failures to recovery probes without changing the cap. Do not promote a challenger: evaluation is not ready and has only 9 paid challenger outcomes. The quality holdout is predictive, not causal, and official stars-rank mapping is unverified.
hypotheses: A bounded repeat-demand coverage response may reduce stockouts, subject to live supply, cash, and refund guards; flat external trade rate and the discoverability block are counterevidence to expanding inventory broadly.

Routing repeated, term-comparable goods price failures to recovery probes may improve learning without changing the price cap; above-cap quotes alone do not establish that any revised offer will convert.
The holdout predictive improvement does not establish causal star gains or verify the official stars-rank mapping.
